subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
Since this is a vehicle rather than a creature, I'm thinking I can skip the usual joint-skeleton setup and just build it as a static prop. I'm sketching out rough dimensions for a pickup truck—around 5.4m long, 2.1m wide, 1.9m tall—to plan the model's proportions.

I'll give it a hovering stance with low glowing thruster pods instead of wheels, keeping the lowest points near ground level. For construction I'm planning to use plain boxes and extrusions for the chassis and hood, sticking to my own paint colors rather than importing from the kit libraries for simplicity.

Still shaping the body profile...

For the bed I'm adding a floor box, side walls, a tailgate, and militarized gear like a roll cage, turret with twin barrels, armor plates, and a missile pod. Then I'm placing four hover pods at the corners as cylindrical nacelles with glowing discs underneath, connected to the chassis via struts.

Positioning the pods so their bottoms sit at ground level, with a cyan glow disc tucked just under the cylinder face, plus a fan intake detail on top using an SVG spoke texture. Now I'm adding neon magenta underglow strips along the sills, glowing headlights and taillights, a grille texture, and door decals with camo stripes, a "07" number, and a skull/hex emblem.

I'm also planning hood scoops, vents, an antenna with a glowing tip, rear thruster ducts with glow on the bed, armored front bull-bar and side skirt plates with bolts, a roof light bar, sensor dome, and skipping vestigial fender arches since there are no wheels. For construction I'm setting up a simple box-building helper function and making sure there's a single root "chassis" joint so the rig requirement of exactly one root joint is satisfied.

I'm adding a turret yaw joint with a child gun pitch joint so those parts can rotate properly, tagging turret parts with the appropriate bone reference. For materials I'm defining custom paint functions that layer grime near the bottom edges and panel wear, using a gunmetal base with hazard yellow, neon cyan, and magenta accent stripes.

Now I'm working out the extrusion geometry for the body and cab, figuring out the thickness axis orientation so everything stays centered at the origin, and sketching the window profile coordinates for the glowing side windows.

Working out the windshield tilt angle...

Now I'm shaping the hood profile tapering from the cab toward the front, sizing the lower chassis box to sit under the hood, and positioning the bed floor panel behind the cab.

Planning the bed walls as thin side boxes and a tailgate panel rather than a solid extruded shape, with a floor panel underneath, then considering wheel-arch pods positioned wider than the body on either side.

I'll make the pods taller, extending from 0 to 0.62 with the fan plane raised accordingly, and consider adding small stabiliser fins as wedge extrusions on each pod. For the glow discs I'll keep them simple, skipping the translucent hover cone idea since it needs alpha, and add a front bumper bar positioned near the nose.

Now I'm shaping an angled prow at the front using an extruded wedge profile in armor color, but realizing it overlaps the grille area I'd planned to place at the hood front — I'll need to adjust the prow's vertical extent so it doesn't completely cover the grille texture plane.

Adding a scoop box with vents on the hood, plus magenta racing stripes across the hood, cab roof, and bed floor via the shared paint function.

For the body paint I'm blending base colors by height with some noise grime, applying magenta stripes near the hood edges, darkening the lower body, and adding teal patches using noise for a weathered cyberpunk mottling effect. Now I'm thinking about door decals as textured planes on the cab sides.

I'm positioning the door emblem below the window line, around y 0.95-1.25, with a hex shield design featuring "07" text, a lightning bolt, and magenta/cyan outlines, making sure the plane orientation on each side reads correctly from the outside.

For the bed sides I'm adding "HEX-7 / MILSEC" text with hazard chevrons on the outer wall faces, then moving on to design the turret: a base ring cylinder for the yaw joint around y 0.8-0.95, topped with a turret body box roughly 0.6x0.35x0.7 in size.

Realizing the bed-mounted turret's forward barrels would clip into the cab, I'm relocating it to the cab roof instead, positioning twin barrels extending forward over the hood above the windshield line, and giving it a railgun look with an ammo drum and glowing muzzle, while the bed gets its own missile pod.

I'm now working out the rear missile rack geometry—angling the tubes upward at the back of the bed and figuring out the rotation math so the rack tilts nose-up correctly along the correct axis.

Then I'm adding a rear main thruster: a glowing cyan cylinder jet positioned at the tailgate, flanked by duct details for the hover vehicle's propulsion.

Now I'm placing red tail light glow boxes near the tailgate corners, plus a roof-mounted light bar with alternating magenta/cyan segments, an antenna rod with a glowing tip, and starting a sensor dome on top.

I'm adding a half-sphere sensor turret on the roof and a roll cage made of hoop bars over the bed, but I need to be careful that these bars attach to the chassis bone rather than accidentally snapping to the nearby turret joint, since nearest-bone logic could misassign them.

Now I'm laying out side skirts with hazard stripe paint, a magenta underglow strip along the body's underside positioned to fit between the wheel pods without too much overlap, and considering whether to add angled armor plates over the fenders before moving on to pylon geometry.

For the pylons, I'm sizing dark connector boxes that bridge from the pods to the body at symmetric x and z offsets. I'm also weighing whether to add small greeble details like bolts or vents versus keeping the part count low, and sketching out curved conduit tubes sweeping from each pod's inner top up toward the body sides, though I'm wary of them clipping through the pylons.

For the texture list, I'm settling on five: grille, fan, door emblem, bed text, and a roof radar pattern, plus a small rear license plate reading "NX-2077" mounted near the tailgate.

Now I'm positioning the plate and side ducts so they don't overlap, and sketching out the fan texture as a dark disc with seven blades and a cyan ring. Writing the box-geometry helper function...

Adding pod details...

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy for the chassis, turret yaw, and gun pitch, defining parent-child relationships and pivot points, then building out the turret's base cylinder and body box geometry.

For the gun assembly, I'm planning twin barrels as rods with flat ends, muzzle brakes, glow rail strips, and coil rings looped around each barrel, plus an ammo box and a glowing red sight camera on the turret. I'm also checking vertical clearances so the turret base, housing, and barrels sit correctly above the cab roof and windshield without clipping.

Now I'm sketching the cab roof plate and reconsidering overall proportions — cab width versus hood width versus bed walls and side pods, landing on a total width around 3.6 for a wing-style pickup build with roughly 2.4 height. For paint, I'm separating body paint from armor paint, using a diagonal modulo pattern on position to generate yellow-and-dark hazard stripes on the skirts.

Checking the lowest points of the geometry (pods, glow discs, skirt rings) to confirm everything sits properly at y=0, then planning the actual code: importing the glow kit and builder utilities, deciding to skip random placement for rivets and bolts since it adds unnecessary complexity, and moving on to writing the grille SVG with a dark background and horizontal cyan slats.

Now I'm working out the emblem SVG — a hexagon outline in cyan with an inner magenta bolt shape and "07" text — plus the bed-side decal with hazard chevrons and "HEX//SEC" text in bold monospace cyan with a magenta underline. I'm also reasoning through the orientation math to make sure the text reads correctly from the viewer's perspective on each side panel.

Now I'm planning the implementation: applying a -20 degree Euler rotation to position the rack tubes correctly, using degree-to-radian conversion for the rotation math.

Checking that the rack geometry fits within the vehicle bounds -- box dimensions, tube placement on the rear face with combined quaternion rotations for tilt, and verifying clearance against the tailgate and cab so it doesn't collide.
